headline: High risk: shared filesystem plus broad network and MCP create prompt-injection, leakage, and action-conflict pathways; Roo Code’s shell/git/browser defaults amplify blast radius.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue and Roo Code both use MCP and share state via filesystem, so attacker-controlled content from one can reach the other through files or tool outputs. Continue treats workspace files as inputs; Roo Code can also read/write workspace files and browse. This is not provably blocked, but the bridge is indirect rather than a guaranteed raw-instruction channel.
conditions: IF either agent writes attacker-controlled text into a shared workspace file and the other agent reads it as instructions, injection is possible.
IF an MCP server returns untrusted content without provenance tags, either agent may follow it.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different workspaces.
Disable MCP servers that return untrusted text.
Require manual review of any file-based handoff.
Use read-only copies for cross-agent sharing.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to all inter-agent artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents read and write workspace files, and both have broad network egress to model providers/MCP servers. Continue touches open editor buffers and workspace files; Roo Code touches VS Code workspace files and browser screenshots. Sensitive code or secrets in the shared workspace can flow into either agent’s outbound API calls, creating a realistic leakage path in default use.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository or workspace, file contents can be exposed to both.
IF either agent sends workspace context to a third-party model provider, shared secrets may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Use separate repos or clones per agent.
Remove secrets from shared workspaces before use.
Restrict outbound model providers to approved endpoints.
Turn on redaction for credentials and tokens.
requires-engineering: enforce per-file access controls between agents.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue and Roo Code both have filesystem write access and both share state via filesystem, while Roo Code additionally has shell, subprocess, install, and git-modification capabilities. In a shared workspace, concurrent edits and git-state changes can overwrite each other or corrupt the repo. The overlap is dangerous by default because no locking is described.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory, file-write races can occur.
IF Roo Code commits or rewrites git state while Continue is editing, conflicts can corrupt work.
IF either agent runs a tool action without coordination, the other may overwrite it.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working tree.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Use git worktrees or branches per agent.
Review diffs before any commit or patch application.
requires-engineering: add workspace locking and optimistic concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can emit code suggestions and tool calls via MCP, and Roo Code can act with shell, browser, and git authority. If Roo Code treats Continue’s output as authoritative, a mistaken or injected suggestion can cascade into real actions such as edits, commits, or browser-driven operations. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier, so the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF Roo Code uses Continue-generated text as a direct plan, downstream actions can be wrong at scale.
IF Continue’s MCP output is not independently checked, Roo Code may execute unsafe edits or commands.
mitigations: Require a human review step before execution.
Force Roo Code to verify claims against files before acting.
Limit Continue to suggestion-only mode for shared tasks.
Disable automatic commit or browser actions.
requires-engineering: add structured, machine-checkable handoff schemas.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and touch source code, but the profiles do not show a residency, certification, or retention mismatch. Continue handles model-provider API keys and Roo Code handles browser screenshots, yet no specific regulated data class or cross-border policy conflict is documented. The other agent is cited because the compliance surface is pairwise, but no breach is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is placed in the shared workspace, a compliance review is required.
IF either agent is configured with a provider or retention policy that differs from the other, mismatch risk increases.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace.
Document provider retention settings for both agents.
Use the same jurisdiction-approved model provider for both.
Review browser screenshot handling before use.
requires-engineering: formalize data-class routing and retention controls.
